pairs.subject: browser-credential-boundary
pairs.evidence: crates/gateway/src/router.rs:15 The completions route spends the person's logged-in claude/codex seats, but nothing checks Host, Origin or X-Forwarded-For before it runs (a grep of crates/gateway for origin/host/forwarded/loopback finds only the default bind string), so a DNS-rebinding page on this machine can drive the seats.

techniques.evidence: crates/gateway/src/main.rs:74 Loopback is only the default. LIGHTTRACK_GATEWAY_BIND accepts any interface without checking it, and the router has no Host/Origin/forwarded-for gate. The technique requires both halves; the gateway has at most the bind half, and only until someone overrides it.

crates/gateway/src/failover.rs:209 Each attempt's raw EngineError text goes back to the caller in lighttrack.attempts on both the 502/503 and the success body. That text comes from failover.rs:172 `error: err.to_string()` and includes upstream BadRequest bodies, CLI stderr and spawn paths. The 'trust boundary you own on both sides' exception does not apply, because the port is reachable from a browser and has no gate.

crates/gateway/src/wire.rs:31 Unknown SDK fields are accepted and dropped, and the gateway builds a typed ChatRequest, so nothing is relayed raw. But the credential spent is the person's ambient CLI login on a loopback service with no caller authentication by design, which the golden path assigns to the loopback-gate shape rather than the browser broker regime.

crates/gateway/src/telemetry.rs:37 The only outbound HTTP destinations are fixed by deployment config (the telemetry URL and engine provider bases). Returned tool_calls go back to the client and are never fetched by the gateway.

crates/gateway/src/router.rs:30 The only operator surface is /health. It is a fixed set of keys that reports whether telemetry is configured as a boolean and never renders requests or credentials. There is no request stream.

pairs.registryProposal: The loopback gate and opaque-errors techniques do not address an OpenAI-compatible local gateway whose callers are other local processes (an SDK base_url) rather than browser pages. A short note on whether opaque-upstream-errors' 'own both sides' exception covers a loopback service only once the loopback gate is in place would make this case decidable.

pairs.subject: browser-credential-boundary
pairs.evidence: clients/typescript/src/index.ts:50 The SDK says it runs in browsers but takes a project key through `apiKey` with no note that a browser-held key is public. A project key can enqueue and read relay tasks (docs/RELAY.md), so a browser app that passes it publishes that power.

techniques.evidence: clients/typescript/src/index.ts:50 The config value is declared bare: nothing says which side it lives on, what an attacker holding it gets, or that it must not ship in a browser bundle. That is despite index.ts:6 advertising 'Node 18+ / browsers'. A grep of src, README and example.ts for bundle/never ship/client-side/expose found no such guidance.
clients/typescript/src/index.ts:661 The SDK is the caller, not a broker. It surfaces the LightTrack API's own response to its own host app, which is not relaying a hidden upstream.

pairs.registryProposal: public-vs-server-env-split is written for an application's env namespace. It has no rule for a client library that runs in both browser and server and accepts a credential option, which is where a privileged key most often ends up in a bundle. A library-side decision rule would help: refuse or warn when a privileged key is configured in a browser runtime, or document a separate publishable key class.
